newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil drowns under arb cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil drowns under arb cargoes.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil market fell as bids were overwhelmed by offers with sellers keen to get rid of arbitrage supplies, traders said on Thursday.
A Singapore trader purchased a total of 490,000 barrels of April gas oil, adding to his earlier purchases of 5.7 million barrels.

They said the trader purchased a 150,000-barrel cargo for April 11-14 loading and another 190,000 barrels for second half April lifting at $27.25 and $26.50 per barrel respectively from a European major. He also bought a 150,000 barrel cargo from Dutch major for April 19-23 loading at $26.90.

Prices were lower, compared to Wednesday's quotes with the onslaught of arbitrage cargoes still taking its toll on prices, traders said. Prices had also lost ground on Wednesday as sellers outnumbered buyers.
"There are just too much supplies on its way here and I do not think he (the local trader) could support prices any further," said a trader with a major oil firm.
Traders said buying interest from the Singapore trader may be wanning, having already bought a total of around 6.2 million barrels.
"I do not expect him to continue buying next week," said one trader.
In the swaps market, jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade traded late afternoon at minus 30 cents on fears that the large prompt physical negative regrade would be extended to April.
The gas oil swaps rebounded slightly with April last quoted at $25.90/$26.00 per barrel up from Wednesday's $25.35/$25.40, brokers said.
